content.text:
I have the full picture. Both governing-law and venue provisions are in the § 26/§ 27 tail (mis-nested under the § 12 heading), and there is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document.

**Analysis:**
- **§ 26 (p0093)** — California law governs ("without respect to principles of conflicts of law").
- **§ 27 (p0094)** — exclusive California state and federal courts (San Luis Obispo County); mutual consent to jurisdiction, waiver of forum objections.
- Searches for "arbitration", "dispute", "court", "injunctive relief" return no competing forum — § 27 is the sole dispute forum, and there is no arbitration seat, foreign or otherwise.

California law + California courts satisfies **both fallback elements** on their material terms. This is not walk-away territory (no non-accepted home jurisdiction, no foreign arbitration). Per the playbook, a clause sitting at the fallback is accepted and is not redlined to reach the preferred New York position.

input.quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
input.rationale: Governing law and venue sit in the unlisted tail (§ 26 at p0093 and § 27 at p0094, mis-nested under the § 12 heading). § 26 selects California law and § 27 fixes the forum "solely and exclusively in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California", with mutual consent to jurisdiction and waiver of venue/forum non conveniens objections. That is California law with the corresponding California courts, which meets both fallback elements on their material terms, so the clause sits at the fallback and we do not redline it up to the preferred New York / New York County position. It is not walk-away territory: searches for arbitration, dispute, court and injunctive relief confirm § 27 is the only dispute forum in the document, there is no arbitration provision or foreign seat, and California is on the accepted list rather than a non-accepted vendor home jurisdiction. Two points are noted only and not flagged: (i) the county chosen is San Luis Obispo, TrueLink's own address (p0003), rather than a neutral or major California venue — but both parties are California-based (Client is in Irvine, California), so there is no material prejudice to us; and (ii) related California-law references appear in § 18 (California UCC), § 23 (Civil Code s.1654 waiver) and § 28 (Civil Code s.1717 fees), which are consistent with the California choice of law and would only need conforming edits if the governing law were ever moved.
